newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent June crude sheds 20 cents after APIs.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent June crude sheds 20 cents after APIs.

text.p: June Brent crude futures prices dropped more than 20 cents on Wednesday in response to a bearish set of API stock data.
June Brent on SIMEX was last traded at $19.40 per barrel, down 22 cents from London, which fell 10 cents overnight to settle at $19.62.
July last traded at $19.24, down 22 cents from London.
API data showed crude stocks rose in the U.S. last week 6.94 million barrels when a 750,000-barrel build had been expected. Gasoline stocks surged 6.5 million, against expectations of 1.0 million.
The surprise data undermined NYMEX on ACCESS and prompted June to test support at $21.00.
The June contract last traded at $21.03, down 35 cents from New York, but the support at $21.00 has held so far.
One broker said the market could look lower since NYMEX has risen strongly in recent days.
"The price fall is quite mild when you consider we have come up a long way," he said. June had gained almost $1 since last week.
